items.title: Onaje Allan Gumbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: The interviewee, Onaje Allan Gumbs, does not mention Monk Rowe in his response. Monk Rowe is identified only as the interviewer and 'old friend' in the boilerplate/intro, but no personal relationship or interaction is described by the interviewee.

ctx.x: Onaje was interviewed in New York City on January 13, 2001, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

My name is Monk Rowe and we are filming in New York City for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive and I’m pleased to have my old friend, Onaje Allan Gumbs with me today, who is a marvelous piano player and arranger and composer, and manages to make a life in music in New York City, which I think is saying something.

Yes, yeah. That’s kind of a mouthful. It’s not the easiest thing to do. But one thing I learned early on, even as a teenager, was the ability to enjoy all genres of music. So jazz has always been my foundation. As a matter of fact my first real introduction to jazz was watching TV and looking at “Peter Gunn” and “Mr. Lucky,” which was scored by Henry Mancini. So needless to say Henry Mancini had an integral part in my development as a musician and a music lover. And I used to go to every film he scored. And…
